about: A three-tool turning program in G-code system A, read with no machine, so every assumed value is the profile's own documented default (plan §8.1, §8.8). It is the golden for what a lathe does differently from a mill: the power-on state is G99 G97 G18 and not G94; the feed unit of a plain F is per revolution; G50 makes its own block's S a clamp and not a speed; G71, G72 and G70 are one-shot cycles, so they show up in `block.cycle` and never in `activeCycle`; G76, G92 and G32 carry a thread lead; and the database has no distance code at all, which is why `distance` is `absolute` although the program never writes G90 (AD-19 rule 8).

states.about: The power-on state, before the program has said anything. Feed per revolution, rpm and the ZX plane are assumed, from the profile; the diameter mode is on, which is what makes X a diameter here.
`G21 G40 G99` states in millimetres what was assumed: G99 is now set, not assumed, and the units come from the program.
A bare T word is the tool change on a turret lathe; the station is the first half of T0101.
AD-19 rule 4: the S of a G50 block is the top speed the spindle may reach under constant surface speed, not a speed to cut at. It is the clamp, and the speed the program is cutting at is still unset.
G96: S is now a surface speed. The clamp of the block above is still what it was.
AD-19 rule 2: G71 is not modal on this control, so it belongs to its own block and to nothing after it. Its F is an ordinary feed per revolution — the roughing feed — and not a thread lead.
Inside the P-Q profile the blocks are ordinary moves again: no cycle is in force and the feed is the finishing feed.
G70 finishes what G71 roughed; it is one-shot in the same way.
`T0100` cancels the offset of station 1 on the way to the retract position. It is not a tool change, so the tool is still the one that was called.
G97 ends constant surface speed: S is revolutions per minute again.
The second block of the two-block G76: its F is the thread lead, not a feed rate. G76 is one-shot here as well, and the flag belongs to this block.
The block after it is an ordinary rapid: the one-shot cycle is over and its F would be a feed again.

In G-code system A, G92 is the single-pass threading cycle and it is modal — which is why the three pass blocks below carry no code of their own. Its F is a lead. On the mill profile the same number is the coordinate-system code, and the database says so there.
A pass block: no code at all, and the modal G92 is still cutting a thread.
AD-19 rule 3: a G00 is a move without a pitch, so it ends the threading cycle.
G32 is a threading move: it becomes the active cycle rather than cancelling one, because its F is a lead.
The tool line carries the station and a rapid on one line.
G83 is a modal drilling cycle on this control, so it stays in force over the C positions below it. Its F is an ordinary feed per revolution.
A bare C position: the cycle repeats at it, so it is still in force.
G80 cancels it.

At the end: the state the program leaves behind. Nothing ever wrote a distance code, and this database has none to write, so absolute is not an assumption but the only reading it allows (AD-19 rule 8).
